steps.title: It was the same Copilot the whole time
say: Look back at Alex's week at Contoso: a proposal in Word, a deck in PowerPoint, metrics in Excel, an inbox cleared in Outlook, a committee caught up on in Teams.
That feels like six different assistants — but was it?
No. It was one Microsoft Copilot, reached six different ways.
One account, one chat history, one set of Pages — which is why nothing ever had to be explained twice.

steps.title: Yesterday's conversation is still there
say: Alex opens the Microsoft Copilot app, and every conversation from the past few weeks is listed down the side.
Today, yesterday, earlier this month — including the chat that started the whole proposal. One click reopens it, mid-thought.
Alex asks where they landed on the pilot scope, and Copilot answers: four weeks, EMEA only, agreed with Priya Nair while drafting Proposal dot docx.
Chat history, saved memories and custom instructions are Alex's own controls under Settings — and an admin can switch the whole thing off for the tenant.

steps.title: Pick the conversation up wherever you already are
say: That thread belongs to Alex's account, not to one browser tab.

Word, Excel and PowerPoint join in through their agents, so the work follows Alex between windows.
Fourteen messages and two attached files — and switching surfaces costs nothing at all.

steps.title: Yesterday's proposal becomes today's deck
say: So what does that continuity actually buy you the next morning?
Yesterday, Alex asked Copilot to create the AI proposal, and got Proposal dot docx — six sections, an executive brief behind every one.
Today the prompt is seven words: turn that proposal into a presentation. No brief re-typed, no files re-attached.
The document, the four-week EMEA pilot, Priya Nair and the September ticket spike all carry over — and Copilot still reads the file from OneDrive under Alex's own permissions.

steps.title: A good answer should not scroll away
say: The paragraph Alex needs for the pilot plan is already buried mid-thread.
One click turns that answer into a Copilot Page — the scope, the success measure and the escalation owner, on a shared canvas.
Priya and three others are editing it at the same time, with Copilot still in the room.
A Page is a real file in Alex's Microsoft 365 container — shared as a link, and covered by sensitivity labels, eDiscovery and export.

steps.title: Chat or Cowork
say: And when the work is bigger than a question?
In Chat, Alex asks where the pilot scope landed, and gets the answer in one turn.
Switch to Cowork, and Alex hands over a whole goal — a brief, the kickoff invite and an agenda for Priya. Cowork plans it, works through it step by step, and stops for Alex's approval.
Underneath, nothing changes: the same sign-in, the same work content, the same permissions. It's the same Copilot, given a bigger job.

steps.title: One assistant. One week. One body of work

All of it came out of one conversation that never had to start over.
The apps were never the point — the work was, and the parts worth keeping became Pages the team still edits.
Alex didn't learn six tools. Alex learned one, and kept every decision along the way.

steps.title: Yesterday's proposal becomes today's deck

チャットでは、Alex がパイロットの範囲がどう決まったかを尋ね、1 回で答えを得ます。 Cowork に切り替えると、Alex は目標まるごとを渡します。概要、キックオフの招待、そして Priya 向けの議題。Cowork はそれを計画し、1 ステップずつ進め、Alex の承認を待って止まります。 その下は何も変わりません。同じサインイン、同じ仕事のコンテンツ、同じアクセス許可。大きな仕事を任された、同じ Copilot です。
